title: Seiras Residences: a tri-key built for renting out in Batu Kawan.
videoTitle: PROPERTY REVIEW #478 | SEIRAS RESIDENCES, BATU KAWAN
excerpt: A 411-unit tower beside UOW Malaysia KDU in Batu Kawan, offering 1,033 sq ft tri-key and dual-key units aimed at students and young engineers. Sean sees a rare Penang project where rent can cover the instalment.
takeaways: Every unit is 1,033 sq ft, either a tri-key with three self-contained rooms or a dual-key.
At about RM600,000, three rooms at about RM1,000 each plus a partitioned room could bring in about RM3,800 a month.
Residents drive through the shops to reach the car park, and much more supply is coming.

sections.heading: What sets it apart
paragraphs: Seiras is a single tower of 411 units, with about 10 shops in front, an eight-level car park, and two layouts of 1,033 sq ft each: a tri-key of three self-contained units, each with its own bathroom and pantry, or a dual-key of a two-bedroom side and a studio. Units come partly furnished with air-conditioners, a kitchen, a smart lock and sub-meters, and each tri-key gets three car parks.

The facilities, about 60,000 sq ft in all, are pitched at young residents: a whole co-working floor, a co-kitchen, a sports lounge, a laundry, a gym, bouldering, pickleball, karaoke and an infinity-edge lap pool.

sections.heading: Where it is
paragraphs: It is the latest phase of the developer's Batu Kawan township, beside UOW Malaysia KDU and opposite the Design Village outlet mall, with the newly completed Columbia Hospital nearby and the Batu Kawan Industrial Park across the road. Shops, groceries and the mall are within walking distance, which Sean thinks makes it one of the few places here a student could live without a car. Roads of six lanes with wide walkways show the scale of the infrastructure.

sections.heading: Rent and returns
paragraphs: Units sell for about RM600,000, about RM600 psf. In the neighbouring Sinaran, rooms let for about RM800 to RM1,200 depending on whether they are partitioned or have their own bathroom, and car parks for about RM120 to RM150. Taking three rooms at about RM1,000 and a partitioned room at RM800, Sean reaches about RM3,800 a month, close to covering the instalment, and the building was nearly topped out, so buyers carry little construction interest.

standout.title: A tri-key drawn on a 3 m grid
standout.body: The structural grid runs about 2.8 to 3 m per bay, giving each unit about 12 m of frontage, so rooms come out at a sensible width and the large centre unit can easily be partitioned again. Its bathroom already has two doors, one from the living area and one from the bed area, which Sean reads as the designers expecting exactly that.

pros: The developer's master plan: the university as the first catalyst, then a hospital, the Design Village, shops, a convention centre and jobs in the industrial park, all on infrastructure far roomier than Penang Island can offer, with road works already preparing for future growth.

A product built for its audience of students and young professionals: a bold tri-key on a sensible grid, about RM3,800 a month if let room by room against the instalment, a whole co-working floor, three car parks per tri-key and an investor-friendly partial fit-out with smart meters. It is not meant for buyers who want to live in it later.
Simplicity: shops, car park, drop-off and one tower, two unit types meant for investment, and only 411 units, one of the lowest densities around.
cons: The driveway: residents must pass through the commercial frontage to reach the car park, as at Sinaran, where double parking is already a problem. He also wishes the eight-level car park had speed ramps, and some may find the concept too plain.
It doesn't suit the typical Batu Kawan buyer who invests first and moves in later, and a tri-key means managing three tenants, though one loan buys the equivalent of three studios.

A lot of upcoming supply, with many high-rises around and more land to develop. Sean anchors on current rents and planned growth such as the third phase of the industrial park, a medical city, a park and an international school, and notes this project's clear focus sets it apart.

closing: A pure investment product for buyers who want one loan to earn three rents in Batu Kawan, not a future family home.
sourceNote: Based on Sean's full English captions for this November 2026 episode and its video description. The 3 on 3 follows the three things he likes and the three he doesn't, in his order, at the end of the video. Sean toured the sales gallery and show units with Michael, who handles viewing appointments for the project; prices and room rents are as Sean quoted them.
